class_id: stage gate requires the value the gated work would supply
symptom: a lifecycle stage is entered only when a fact is already present, and the work that would SUPPLY that fact is due only at or after that stage — a deadlock. Every entity that cannot obtain the fact by some other route is stuck at the earlier stage forever, with no error, no retry exhaustion and no blocked row: the gated work is simply never due, so nothing is tracked as missing. The tell is a perfect correlation between having the fact and having the downstream artefacts, with no scatter — a budget, ordering or retry problem produces a spread, a gate produces a clean split. Universal shape: any promotion condition that reads an output of the work it gates. The bug hides when an incidental side channel supplies the fact for most entities, making a systematic gate look like an intermittent minority bug.
first_seen: 2026-09-19 (staging). `deriveLifecycleStage` returns PRE_OPEN only when `priceRangeMin > 0` (stage-reconciler.ts:161); `STAGE_DOCUMENT_TYPES.UPCOMING = ['DRHP']` while PRICE_BAND_AD first becomes due at PRE_OPEN (document-state-machine.ts:85-102). So: no band -> stage UPCOMING -> PRICE_BAND_AD never due -> the advertisement that carries the band is never fetched -> no band. Measured across all 16 UPCOMING IPOs: 14 of 14 WITH a band had 6 fetch-state rows; 2 of 2 WITHOUT a band (Anand Seamless opening 09-22, Liqvd Digital opening 09-23) had exactly 1 row (DRHP), zero documents, and would have reached their open date with a blank price band. Most IPOs escape only because exchange board data happens to carry the band | AUDIT 2026-09-19 before proposing a fix, which found two holes in the first proposal: (a) only `offering_type='IPO'` ever holds a PRICE_BAND_AD (21 of 21); every non-IPO type stores min=max (TENDER 16/16, RIGHTS 5/5, NCD 3/3, INVITS 3/3, BUYBACK 1/1, REITS 1/1) - a single fixed price in both columns, never a range - so a naive 'no band -> fetch the band ad' rule chases a document that cannot exist. The existing `isFixedPrice` guard excludes them only when a price is PRESENT: with a NULL band it is false, so 24 rows (19 OFS, 4 NCD, 1 RIGHTS) escape it and would hunt a non-existent document - an explicit offering-type guard is required as well. (b) 2 of 16 live UPCOMING IPOs have NO `open_date` (Adroit Industries, Swastika Infra), so a rule keyed only on open_date proximity would silently never fire for them - the same never-fires shape as the bug. (c) N MEASURED 2026-09-19 across MANY IPOs, after a first proposal of N=5 that was INVENTED (reasoned from the SEBI ~2-working-day requirement, zero IPOs behind it) and was correctly challenged by the owner. `documents.filing_date` is 0 of 21 populated so the true FILING-to-open window is still underivable; `field_sources` however holds 620 band-provenance rows across 310 IPOs with timestamps. Three nested populations, each cleaner: ALL 310 IPOs -> median -30 days, min -2085, because 242 of 310 bands were recorded AFTER the IPO opened (historical backfill, not observation - a median from this population describes our scraping history, not IPO behaviour). LIVE-WATCHED (IPO row created before open, gap 0-60d), n=67 -> median 5, p90 7, max 12; still partly confounded, 20 of 67 had the band written the same day we first saw the IPO. BAND WATCHED ARRIVING (IPO known >=2 days before the band row appeared), n=17 -> median 4, p25 1, p90 5.8, max 7; distribution 0d:2, 1d:3, 2d:3, 4d:4, 5d:3, 7d:2. READING: the spread is wide and the LOW end is what matters - 5 of 17 (29%) had their band recorded 0-1 days before open, so a window set at the MEDIAN would promote too late for nearly a third of IPOs. Set N from the upper end (>=7) : being early costs a few NOT_YET_FILED fetch attempts, which the state machine already handles; being late costs a blank price band on a live IPO. CAVEAT: this measures when WE RECORDED the band, not when the issuer FILED it, so it is a LOWER bound on earliness - the true filing is at or before our recording, which pushes N up, never down, and that direction is safe.
fix_prs: none yet - #795. Initial RCA blamed budget starvation (`UPCOMING_RESERVE_SLOTS = 1` vs 2 candidates) and was WRONG: #468's reservation is ON and firing (`upcomingReserved:1`), the two IPOs were visited 23 times in 78 elapsed cycles, and on every one of those visits `dueDocTypesForStage('UPCOMING')` returned `['DRHP']` only, so no PRICE_BAND_AD row could ever be created. Raising the slot count would have changed nothing. FIX RULE (generic): a promotion condition must depend only on facts our own pipeline cannot suppress - never on an output of the work it gates. Applied here: (1) applicability FIRST, reusing `notApplicableTypes()`/`deriveIssueShape()` plus an explicit offering-type guard (see the measurement below - the existing `isFixedPrice` guard does NOT cover a null-band non-IPO row); (2) promote on whichever signal exists - `open_date` within N days when present, an RHP on file, or the issue appearing on an exchange board; (3) never promote on the price band itself; (4) null-safe by construction - an issue with NO available signal stays UPCOMING and is REPORTED as unresolvable rather than silently stalling, which is the difference between a visible gap and the bug this class describes
detection_check: none. Every existing document check JOINs `document_fetch_state` and can only grade rows that EXIST (see failure class `check-blind-to-a-row-never-created`), and here the row is never created because the type is never due. Proposed `m_upcoming_missing_price_band_tracking` (#796) is entity-anchored and catches it: live IPO opening within 7 days with no PRICE_BAND_AD fetch-state row; verified to flag exactly the 2 and pass the other 18 of 20
